name: Discontinued Tech
description: Software, gadgets and websites that millions used and that no longer exist, each from launch to shutdown.

checkpoints.name: Tapes and discs
checkpoints.note: The floppy disk, the video cassette and the portable CD player belong to the years when software and films came on something you could hold. All of them are gone now.

checkpoints.name: The dial-up web
checkpoints.note: Netscape, GeoCities, AltaVista, ICQ and Napster are among the first names millions of people meet online. None of them survives in its first form.

checkpoints.name: The broadband years
checkpoints.note: The iPod, Windows XP, Skype and the first social networks arrive. So do Friendster, Orkut and the Zune, which lose to stronger rivals.

checkpoints.name: After the iPhone
checkpoints.note: The iPhone of 2007 has no keyboard and will not run Flash. Within a few years BlackBerry, Symbian, Windows Phone and the web plug-ins are on their way out.

checkpoints.name: The 2020s
checkpoints.note: Flash is switched off at the end of 2020, Internet Explorer and the iPod are retired in 2022, and Skype closes in 2025.
